newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents lower Friday, although some traders said the market was likely to come in closer to unchanged after Thursday's finish off the lows.
New York arabica futures ended mixed yesterday, with September settling down 1.25 cents at 180.40 cents a lb but well above the low of 174.25 cents. The back months closed up 1.00 to 3.90.
"September close over 180 yesterday, so it is kind of constructive," said one trader.
The September/December switch narrowed to 20.10 cents from 23.50 cents at the close Wednesday.
On the charts, traders pegged September resistance at the Wednesday and Thursday high of 184.50, followed by 192.00 to 193.00 cents. Support was seen at 176.00, then 174.25 cents.
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks dipped by 252 60-kg bags as of July 23, to 90,645 bags. An additional 1,489 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, Weather Services Corp said on Friday that there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt. It said low temperatures would be near normal levels through early next week and warm to above normal levels by the middle of the week.

London coffee futures were higher early Friday, buoyed by light trade buying. At the midday break, September was $31 higher, at $1,610, after ranging from $1,617 to $1,600. November rose $38, to $1,608.
